# Add a tool to the Venira MCP server

New tools must look and behave like the existing ones, because clients and agents rely on consistent descriptions, schemas, and error shapes. Learn the conventions from the code, then copy them.

## 1. Learn the conventions first

- `project_recent_files` and `project_list_files` on the `tools/`, `lib/`, and `scripts/verify/` folders.
- Read one or two tools close to the new one (for example a small read-only tool and a mutating one) with `project_read_batch`.
- Find where tools are registered: `project_search` (kind `literal_content`) for an existing tool name, and follow it to the registry.
- Note the helpers the existing tools share: workspace path validation, error codes, audit logging, output-mode trimming.

## 2. Design the tool

- Name: `project_<verb>_<noun>`, consistent with neighbours.
- Description: follow the house style seen in existing tools: one line of what it does, then `Use when:`, `Avoid when:`, and `Output:`.
- Input schema: bounded numbers (min/max), `0/1` flags the way existing tools do them, and an optional `reason` for the audit log if the tool mutates anything.
- Decide read-only vs mutating up front. Mutating tools need path safety and snapshot or rollback advice in their description.

## 3. Implement

Checkpoint first with `project_snapshot` (include the registry file, README, and CHANGELOG in `paths`). Then create the tool file with `project_write_file` (`mode=create`) and register it with `project_edit_file`. Reuse shared helpers instead of re-implementing path checks or error handling.

## 4. Verify

- Add a case to the matching script under `scripts/verify/` (or a dedicated test script) covering success, a not-found or invalid input, and any size limits.
- Run the type-check/build and the verify script with `project_shell_run`. Feed failures to `project_explain_error`.
- Run the project's doctor or consistency script if one exists, since it often cross-checks the tool list against docs.

## 5. Document

Update the README tool list and add a CHANGELOG entry. Then review everything with `project_git_diff` and report: tool name, files touched, snapshot id, and which checks passed.

# Venira coding workflow

Venira tools make edits auditable and reversible. Follow this loop so every change is small, checkpointed and verified, and a mistake costs one restore instead of an hour of cleanup.

Clients may prefix tool names (for example `mcp__venira__project_read_file`). The `project_*` part is the stable name.

## Ground rules

- Stay inside the workspace. Paths are workspace-relative; forward slashes work on Windows too.
- Read before you write. Never edit from memory of a file. Re-read when anything else may have touched it.
- Make the smallest change that solves the task. No drive-by reformatting or unrelated cleanups.
- Never put secrets in files, commands or chat. Store tokens with `project_secret` (prefer `value_env`) and inject them with `secret_env` on `project_shell_run`.
- Delete, overwrite, move-over and destructive git operations only when the user asked, and only after a snapshot.
- If intent is ambiguous and the change is hard to undo, ask one short question. Otherwise proceed and state your assumptions in the report.

## 1. Orient

- `project_recent_files` (depth 2-3, limit 20-30) shows what moved lately and which files are in play.
- In an unfamiliar area, `project_plan_read_batch` with a one-line task description, then run the `project_read_batch` it proposes (max 8 files per call).
- For big files use `project_outline_symbol` first, then `project_read_file` with `start_line`/`end_line` or `ranges`.
- Never guess paths. Use `project_search` (`file_name`, `literal_content`, `definition`) or `project_list_files`.
- Read project instructions if they exist (AGENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, README) before the first edit.

## 2. Checkpoint

Create a snapshot (`project_snapshot`, `action=create`, narrow `paths`, label like `before <what>`) before edits that span several files, deletes, moves or overwrites of anything git does not hold, and large refactors. Skip it for a tiny single-file edit already covered by git. Check `truncated` and `skipped` in the result, and keep the snapshot id for the report and for any rollback (see §5).

## 3. Edit

| Need | Tool |
|---|---|
| One targeted change | `project_edit_file` with exact `old_text`, plus `expected_sha256`; use `edits[]` for several replacements in one file |
| Several files that must land together | `project_edit_batch` (all-or-nothing, automatic rollback) |
| Change that arrives as a diff | `project_apply_patch`, `dry_run=1` first |
| New file | `project_write_file` `mode=create`, `create_dirs=1` |
| Replace a whole file | `project_write_file` `mode=overwrite` with `expected_sha256`, after a snapshot |
| Rename or move | `project_move_path` (not undoable, snapshot first) |
| Duplicate | `project_copy_path` |
| Delete | `project_delete_path` (`recursive=1` for folders), only on request, snapshot first |

Before changing a shared symbol, signature or file name, run `project_change_impact` (pass `symbols` or `files`) to list dependents and the tests affected. Pass a short `reason` on mutating calls so the audit trail explains why.

## 4. Verify

- Review the change with `project_git_diff` (`include_patch=1`) or `project_diff_files`.
- Run the narrowest check first (type-check or one test), then the full suite once before finishing. Use `project_shell_run` with `background=0` for short commands. For long ones use `background=1`, then `project_shell_status` with `wait_seconds` until `running=false`.
- Pick the shell explicitly when syntax matters. Windows PowerShell 5.1 has no `&&`: chain with `;`, or use `pwsh` or `bash`.
- On failure, pass the stderr to `project_explain_error`, confirm the cause in the code, then fix. Do not retry blindly.
- Fix and re-verify until clean. If you cannot run a check, say so instead of implying it passed.

## 5. Roll back

`project_snapshot` `action=restore` with the id: first `dry_run=1` to preview, then `verify=1`. Use `paths` to restore only some files. Use `delete_extra=1` only when you really want files created after the snapshot removed. Restore beats hand-reverting because it is exact.

## Error recovery

| Signal | Meaning | Do this |
|---|---|---|
| `not_found` | Wrong path | `project_search` for the name. Do not guess. |
| `old_text_not_found` | File changed, or whitespace or line endings differ | Read `data.mismatch` and `data.context`, re-read that range, retry with exact text |
| `old_text_ambiguous` | Text matches several places | Widen `old_text` with surrounding lines. `replace_all=1` only if every match should change |
| `expected_sha256` refused | File changed since you read it | Re-read, re-apply the change. Never force it |
| `conflict` | Target already exists | Choose another path, or snapshot then `overwrite` if intended |
| `batch_failed` | Everything was rolled back (`rollback_succeeded`) | Fix the item named in `data.executed` and `data.skipped`, rerun the batch |
| `approval_required` | A human must approve | Tell the user, give `data.approval.approve_command` or use `approval_wait_ms`, retry once with `approval_id`. Do not work around it |
| `repeated_failure` | The identical command already failed | Read `data.previous.stderr_tail` and change the command. `retry_failed=1` only for flaky or environmental failures |
| `truncated: true` | Output was cut | Continue with `start_line=next_start_line`, or narrow `relative_path`, `limit` or `depth` |
| Odd or stale results | Cache out of sync after external changes | `project_cache_clear`, then `project_health` (sections `warnings`, `posture`) |

A `trimmed` flag or "Output mode compact" hint only means the payload was shortened. It is not an error.

## Final report

Keep it short and factual: files changed, snapshot id (if any), checks run and their result, and anything left undone or assumed.

name: venira-debug-ci
description: Diagnose and fix failing builds, tests, type errors, and CI runs using Venira tools (project_explain_error, project_ci_status, project_ci_logs, project_ci_wait, project_ci_control). Use this skill whenever the user reports a red build, failing test, CI failure, a stack trace or error message, "lỗi build", "CI fail", or asks why a pipeline or command broke, even if they only paste an error.
---

# Debug builds and CI with Venira

Find the root cause from evidence (logs, error text), fix it, and prove the fix. Retrying without reading the log wastes CI minutes and hides real problems.

## 1. Get the evidence

- Local failure: reproduce with `project_shell_run` (`background=0` for short commands). Capture the stderr tail.
- CI failure: `project_ci_status` with `pr`, `branch`, or `ref` to find the failing run. Pass `run_id` to see its jobs, then `project_ci_logs` with the failing `job_id` (start with the default tail, widen `tail_lines` only if needed).

## 2. Classify the failure

Pass the error block to `project_explain_error`. It matches known signatures (TypeScript, Python, git, npm, GitHub) offline and returns likely cause plus next actions. Treat that as a hypothesis and confirm it against the code:
- Locate the failing file and line with `project_search` and `project_read_file` (ranges).
- If the failure points at a changed symbol, check `project_change_impact`.
- Separate three causes: a code bug, a flaky or environment problem (timeouts, network, cache), and a config or dependency drift. Each has a different fix.

## 3. Fix

Follow the venira-coding-workflow habits: snapshot if the fix is multi-file, edit surgically, then re-run the exact failing command locally. If `project_shell_run` answers `repeated_failure`, read `data.previous.stderr_tail` and change the approach instead of passing `retry_failed=1`.

## 4. Confirm on CI

- Push (via `project_shell_run`, e.g. `git push`), then `project_ci_wait` on the branch or PR. If `terminal=false`, call again with the same selector.
- Use `project_ci_control` with `retry_failed` only for confirmed flaky jobs, and always give a `reason`.
- Use `project_ci_trigger` only when a workflow supports manual dispatch or no new commit is available.

## Report

State the root cause in one or two sentences, the fix, and the evidence that it works (local command result and CI overall status). If it was flaky or environmental, say so plainly rather than claiming a code fix.

# Git and PR workflow with Venira

Make each step explicit and reversible. Merging and pushing change shared state, so do them only when the user asked.

## 1. Inspect

Call `project_git_status` (branch, ahead/behind, changed files) and `project_git_diff` to see exactly what would be committed. Use `project_git_log` for recent commit style so new messages match the repo.

## 2. Branch

- New work goes on a branch: `project_git_branch` action `create` (optionally `from`), then `switch`.
- Need to pause? `project_git_stash` push (add `include_untracked=1` when needed), then `apply` over `pop` so a copy is kept until you are sure.

## 3. Commit

- Stage and commit with `project_git_commit`, passing explicit `paths` so unrelated files stay out.
- Write an imperative subject line, matching the repo's convention from the log. Put the why in the body.
- Amend only when the user asks. Never use it to rewrite commits that were already pushed.

## 4. Push and open the PR

`project_git_commit` does not push. Push with `project_shell_run` (`git push -u origin <branch>`). Under the current policy: plain push is allowed without approval everywhere except `strict` (needs approval there); force pushes (`--force`, `+ref`, `--force-with-lease`), delete pushes, `--mirror`, and pushes to URLs need approval in `balanced` and `strict`, and run freely in `permissive` and `off`. If one asks for approval, tell the user instead of trying to dodge it.

Then `project_pr_create` with a one-line imperative title and a body holding a summary and a test plan. Use `draft=1` if the work is unfinished.

## 5. Watch CI and respond

- `project_ci_wait` with the `pr` selector. On failure, switch to the venira-debug-ci skill.
- Reply to reviewers with `project_pr_comment` (use `path` and `line` for inline notes).
- `project_pr_close` / `project_pr_reopen` for abandoned or mistakenly closed PRs.

## 6. Merge only on request

Merge with `project_pr_merge` only when the user asked and `project_ci_status` is green. Ask or infer the method (`merge`, `squash`, `rebase`) and whether to delete the branch. Report the resulting sha.
